notes: All years are IFRS; the BMW Group has prepared IFRS consolidated statements for the whole 2007-2025 window, so there is no standard change to flag.
revenue is total Group revenue, i.e. including the Financial Services segment (not automotive-only).
operatingIncome is 'Profit before financial result (EBIT)' (called 'Earnings before financial result' up to 2016).

netIncome is profit attributable to shareholders of BMW AG, not total net profit for the year. The difference is the non-controlling interests: FY2025 total net profit EUR 7,451m vs EUR 7,294m attributable; FY2020 EUR 3,857m vs EUR 3,775m.
totalEquity is equity attributable to shareholders of BMW AG (FY2025 total equity incl. non-controlling interests EUR 97,906m vs EUR 95,697m attributable).

totalDebt is the sum of the balance-sheet lines 'Financial liabilities' (non-current) and 'Financial liabilities' (current). BMW itself discloses this total in its financial-position analysis (e.g. FY2025: EUR 110,469m, 41.5% of total assets). It therefore includes lease liabilities and Financial Services refinancing, so it is much larger than a pure bond/bank-loan figure.

operatingCashFlow is the Group 'cash inflow from operating activities' from the consolidated cash flow statement. BMW also publishes an Automotive-segment figure (e.g. FY2015 EUR 11,836m and FY2007-EUR 6,246m); that segment number is NOT used here, which is why the early years look large relative to later ones (the Group figure is dominated by the Financial Services segment's leased-product and sales-financing flows).

capex is BMW's own 'capital expenditure (excluding capitalised development costs)' = investments in property, plant and equipment and other intangible assets, excluding capitalised development costs, shown negative. Capitalised development costs are reported separately by BMW (FY2025: total investment in intangible assets and PP&E per the cash flow statement EUR 10,963m, of which EUR 3,726m capitalised development costs; the capex figure used here is EUR 7,237m). The same definition is used for every year so the series is comparable. Cash-flow-statement capex on the 'total investment in intangible assets and property, plant and equipment' line is EUR 10,963m (2025) and EUR 12,205m (2024).

sharesOutstanding = ordinary shares plus preferred shares in circulation at 31 December (issued less treasury shares). For 2007-2010 the reports give the number of shares in thousands (601,995k ordinary plus 52,196k/52,665k/53,163k preferred); from 2011 the statement of changes in equity gives exact figures. From 2022 the count falls sharply because of the share buyback programme (601,995,196 ordinary -> 554,226,093 at 31.12.2025).

dilutedEPS is the basic/diluted earnings per ordinary share. BMW states that diluted earnings per share equal basic earnings per share in every year of the window. Preferred-share EPS is about EUR 0.02 higher.
dividendPerShare is the dividend per ordinary share for the fiscal year (proposal of the Board of Management for the latest year). The preferred share receives EUR 0.02 more.

Restatements applied: 2013 was restated in the Annual Report 2014 under IAS 8 (net profit 5,314 -> 5,303; operating cash flow 3,614 -> 4,127; EPS 8.10 -> 8.08; equity 35,455 -> 35,412). Equity for 2012 was restated from EUR 30,295m to 30,499m in the Annual Report 2013. 2017 was restated in the Annual Report 2018 (EPS 13.12 -> 13.07, attributable profit 8,620 -> 8,589, equity 54,112 -> 53,772). 2018 was adjusted for the first-time adoption of IFRS 16 in the Annual Report 2019 (attributable profit 7,117 -> 6,974; EPS 10.82 -> 10.60; equity 57,559 -> 57,268). 2021 operating cash flow was restated from 15,903 to 15,914 in the 2022 report. 2024 employees were restated from 159,104 to 157,457 after non-consolidated companies were excluded from 2025 onwards. BMW also restates prior years for presentation changes of 'minor importance' (footnote 1 of the 2025 ten-year comparison).

Employee counts are not fully comparable across the window: up to 2019 temporary staff, interns and apprentices were included (the 2019 figure was adjusted to 133,778 to remove them), and from 2025 non-consolidated companies are excluded.

Cross-check against the Yahoo figures in docs/global-companies/snapshot-2026-10-26.json (converted at the snapshot FX rate of 1.1199 USD/EUR, which is only a rough conversion for older years): FY2025 revenue EUR 134.9bn vs 133.5bn here (+1.1%), net income 7.37bn vs 7.29bn (+1.1%), EBIT 10.09bn vs 10.19bn (-0.9%); FY2024 137.3bn vs 142.4bn (-3.5%, explained by the EUR/USD move between the 2024 average and today's rate); FY2023 net income 10.94bn vs 11.29bn and FY2022 16.85bn vs 17.94bn, likewise FX. No scope or line-item differences found. Two deliberate definition differences remain: Yahoo's totalAssets for FY2025 is about EUR 279bn against BMW's balance-sheet total of EUR 266bn, and Yahoo's totalDebt is about EUR 93bn against the EUR 110bn balance-sheet financial liabilities used here; both come from Yahoo's own derivation, not from BMW's statements.
